label: mode_equivalence
question: Do gather and sparse produce the same spikes on the real P1 subset at the restored window, or only on fixtures?
method: Forward only under no_grad, 300 steps, batch 1, rank 8, identical tonic drive of 20.0 mV on the first 1042 columns, same seed for both couplings.
verdict: The modes are interchangeable on the real subset at this window.

saturation_check.what_was_claimed: That the real arm runs at an active fraction of 0.81 against a 0.25 ceiling, i.e. saturated.
saturation_check.why_it_was_wrong: This script drove drive[:, :, :1042] -- the first 1042 POSITIONS in sorted root_id order -- not the 1042 neurons select_io_indices identifies as inputs. Current was injected into the wrong neurons, so the 0.8115 figure describes a configuration the experiment never runs. It is the same positional-versus-label confusion the codebase warns about at run_pilot.py, arrived at independently.
saturation_check.correct_measurement: data/results/drive_at_window_v783.json, via controls.activity_profile with the real input and readout indices: at drive 20.0 and 300 steps the active fraction is 0.1762 for real, 0.2104 for shuffled and 0.6037 for random.

note_on_the_equivalence_result: The indexing error does not touch the equivalence finding, which compares the two modes against each other under one identical drive. Whatever neurons were driven, both modes were driven the same way and produced byte-identical rasters.
